title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit that turns on the main radiator cooling fan. If the fan does not run, the engine can overheat when you are stopped or in slow traffic.
symptoms: Engine runs hot in traffic or at idle
Fan runs all the time, or never runs

causes.name: Damaged wiring or melted connector at the fan

checks: Turn on the A/C and see whether the cooling fans come on
Check the cooling fan fuses and relays
Check for power and ground at the fan connector
fix: Usually a new fan relay or fan motor, or a wiring repair at the fan connector.

cost.job: Replace cooling fan motor or fan assembly

drive: Watch the temperature gauge closely. Highway driving may be fine since moving air cools the radiator, but in traffic or at idle it can overheat. If the gauge climbs toward hot or you see steam, pull over and shut it off; overheating can ruin the engine. Get it fixed soon.
test_first: Check the fan fuse and relay, command fan 1 with a scan tool, check power and ground at the fan motor, and inspect the connector for melting before replacing the motor or module.

title: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the second cooling fan, or the high-speed fan circuit on some vehicles. Without it the engine may run hot in traffic and the A/C may blow warm.
symptoms: Engine runs hot in traffic or at idle
Fan runs all the time, or never runs

causes.name: Damaged wiring or melted connector at the fan

checks: Turn on the A/C and see whether the cooling fans come on
Check the cooling fan fuses and relays
Check for power and ground at the fan connector
fix: Usually a new fan relay or fan motor, or a wiring repair.

cost.job: Replace cooling fan motor or fan assembly

drive: Watch the temperature gauge closely. Highway driving may be fine since moving air cools the radiator, but in traffic or at idle it can overheat. If the gauge climbs toward hot or you see steam, pull over and shut it off; overheating can ruin the engine. Get it fixed soon.
test_first: Check the fan fuse and relay, command fan 2 with a scan tool, check power and ground at the fan motor, and inspect the connector for melting before replacing the motor or module.

title: Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the third cooling fan speed or fan on vehicles that have one.
symptoms: Engine may run hot in traffic
A/C may blow warm at idle
checks: Turn on the A/C and see whether the cooling fans come on
Check the cooling fan fuses and relays
Check for power and ground at the fan connector
fix: Usually a new fan relay or fan motor, or a wiring repair.

cost.job: Replace cooling fan motor or fan assembly

title: Cooling Fan Rationality Check
plain: The computer turned the cooling fan on but did not see the engine temperature or fan speed respond the way it expected.
symptoms: Engine may run hot in traffic
Fan may run weakly or not at all

causes.name: Worn or weak cooling fan motor
Failed fan relay or control module
Low coolant or other cooling system problem

checks: Check that the fans run at full speed when commanded
Check coolant level and look for other cooling codes
fix: Usually a new cooling fan motor or control module.

cost.job: Replace cooling fan motor or fan assembly

title: Cooling Fan Circuit Over Current
plain: The cooling fan circuit is drawing more current than it should, which usually means the fan motor is binding or shorted.
symptoms: Engine may run hot in traffic
checks: Spin the fan by hand with the engine off and key out to feel for binding
Measure fan current draw
fix: Usually a new cooling fan motor.

cost.job: Replace cooling fan motor or fan assembly

title: Cooling Fan Power/Ground Circuit
plain: The computer sees a problem with the power or ground supply to the cooling fan.
symptoms: Engine may run hot in traffic

causes.name: Blown fan fuse or failed relay

checks: Check the fan fuse and relay
Check power and ground at the fan connector
fix: Usually a fuse, relay, ground or connector repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: The computer sees a general electrical problem with the second EGR sensor, used on some engines to monitor EGR position or flow.
checks: Check the sensor reference voltage, ground and signal
Inspect wiring near the hot exhaust
fix: Usually a new sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Throttle Control Circuit "A" Open
plain: Some engines, mostly diesels, use a throttle plate to help pull exhaust gas into the intake. The computer sees an open circuit to that throttle.
checks: Inspect the connector at the EGR or intake throttle
Check the motor resistance and wiring
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new throttle valve assembly.

cost.job: Replace EGR or intake throttle valve

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Throttle Control Circuit "A" Range/Performance
plain: The EGR throttle plate is not moving to the position the computer asks for, usually because soot is making it stick.

causes.name: Soot or carbon buildup on the throttle plate
Failing throttle motor or position sensor

checks: Inspect the throttle plate for soot and clean it
Command the throttle with a scan tool and watch actual position
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR or intake throttle valve.

cost.job: Replace EGR or intake throttle valve

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "A" Control Circuit Low
plain: The circuit that controls the EGR valve is reading lower voltage than it should, which usually points to a short or a failed EGR valve.
checks: Check the EGR valve resistance
Check the wiring for chafing or a short to ground
fix: Usually a new EGR valve or solenoid, or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "A" Control Circuit High
plain: The circuit that controls the EGR valve is reading higher voltage than it should, often from an open wire or a failed EGR valve.
checks: Check the EGR valve resistance and connector
Check for power at the connector with the key on
fix: Usually a new EGR valve or solenoid, or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve "A" Stuck Closed
plain: The computer thinks the exhaust pressure control valve is stuck closed, which traps exhaust and can cut power and raise exhaust temperatures.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels

causes.name: Valve seized closed by soot or rust

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Usually freeing up or replacing the valve or actuator.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
plain: The computer sees an electrical problem with the sensor that reports where the exhaust pressure control valve is.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels

causes.name: Failed position sensor (often built into the valve actuator)

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new valve actuator or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The exhaust pressure control valve position reading does not match what the valve should be doing.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels
checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Usually freeing up or replacing the valve or actuator.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
plain: The exhaust pressure control valve position sensor signal is lower than possible.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels
checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Replace the actuator or sensor, or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
plain: The exhaust pressure control valve position sensor signal is higher than possible.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels
checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Replace the actuator or sensor, or repair the wiring.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The exhaust pressure control valve position signal is cutting in and out or jumping around.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels
checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch its position reading
Inspect the position sensor connector and wiring
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the actuator.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
plain: The system that blows fresh air into the bank 1 exhaust after a cold start is not moving enough air. It helps the catalytic converter warm up and does not affect normal driving.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Air pump may sound loud or be silent on cold start

causes.name: Carbon-blocked air passages in the head or exhaust
Blown fuse or bad pump relay

checks: Listen for the air pump after a cold start
Check the pump fuse and relay
Inspect the check (combi) valve and hoses for moisture, carbon or cracks
fix: Usually a new air pump, a new check (combi) valve, or clearing blocked passages.
examples: Common on older VW and Audi models with a clogged or failed combi valve
drive: Usually you can keep driving; this system mainly cuts emissions for the first minute or so after a cold start. Get it repaired before an emissions test. If you notice a burning smell near the pump or the fuse keeps blowing, get it checked sooner.
test_first: Check the fuse and relay, test pump output on a cold start, check the bank 1 check valve and air passages for carbon or blockage, and inspect hoses before replacing the pump.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 2)
plain: The system that blows fresh air into the bank 2 exhaust after a cold start is not moving enough air.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Air pump may sound loud or be silent on cold start

causes.name: Carbon-blocked air passages in the head or exhaust
Blown fuse or bad pump relay

checks: Listen for the air pump after a cold start
Check the pump fuse and relay
Inspect the check (combi) valve and hoses for moisture, carbon or cracks
fix: Usually a new air pump, a new check (combi) valve, or clearing blocked passages.
drive: Usually you can keep driving; this system mainly cuts emissions for the first minute or so after a cold start. Get it repaired before an emissions test. If you notice a burning smell near the pump or the fuse keeps blowing, get it checked sooner.
test_first: Check the fuse and relay, test pump output on a cold start, check the bank 2 check valve and air passages for carbon or blockage, and inspect hoses before replacing the pump.

title: Fan Overspeed
plain: The engine cooling fan is spinning faster than the computer commanded, which on trucks with a clutch fan often means the fan clutch is locked up.

causes.name: Fan control solenoid or wiring fault

checks: Check whether the fan clutch or fan speed changes as the engine warms up
Check the fan speed sensor and wiring
fix: Usually a new fan clutch, or a new fan speed sensor.

title: Fan Speed Low
plain: The engine cooling fan is spinning slower than the computer expects, so the engine may not get enough cooling at low speed.
symptoms: Engine runs hot in traffic or while towing
A/C may blow warm at idle

causes.name: Faulty fan speed sensor or wiring

checks: Check whether the fan clutch or fan speed changes as the engine warms up
Check the fan speed sensor and wiring
fix: Usually a new fan clutch or fan motor.

title: Fan Speed High
plain: The engine cooling fan is spinning faster than expected or its speed signal reads too high.
checks: Check whether the fan clutch or fan speed changes as the engine warms up
Check the fan speed sensor and wiring
fix: Usually a new fan clutch or fan speed sensor.

title: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
plain: Fuel vapors are being pulled into the engine when they should not be, usually because the purge valve is stuck open. This can make the engine hard to start right after filling up.
symptoms: Hard starting or stalling right after refueling

causes.name: Purge valve leaking when it should be closed
Charcoal canister damaged, sending charcoal into the purge line

checks: Check if the purge valve holds vacuum with the engine off
Look for charcoal granules in the purge hose
Watch fuel tank pressure while the purge valve is commanded closed
fix: Usually a new purge valve; also replace the canister if it is leaking charcoal.
examples: Often seen on GM cars and trucks when the purge valve sticks open
drive: Usually you can keep driving, but if the engine stalls or won't start right after refueling, get it checked soon, since a stall in traffic is risky. If you smell strong raw fuel or see a leak, stop driving and get it looked at.
test_first: Check whether the purge valve seals when it should be closed, look for charcoal in the purge line, and test the tank pressure sensor before replacing the canister or valve.

title: Evaporative Emission System Low Purge Flow
plain: Less fuel vapor than expected is being drawn from the charcoal canister into the engine, usually because the purge valve or a hose is blocked.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blocked, kinked or disconnected purge hose
Wiring fault to the purge valve

checks: Command the purge valve open and check for vacuum at the canister side
Inspect purge hoses for kinks or blockage
Check the purge valve wiring
fix: Usually a new purge valve or a hose repair.
drive: Usually safe to keep driving; this is an emissions-system fault that rarely changes how the car runs. Make sure the gas cap is on tight. If you smell strong raw fuel or see fuel leaking, stop driving and get it checked right away because of the fire risk.
test_first: Command the purge valve and confirm flow, check the purge hose for kinks or disconnection and the canister for clogging, and check the wiring before replacing parts.

title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
plain: The circuit for the EVAP vent valve is reading lower voltage than it should, usually from a short or a failed valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives

causes.name: Corroded connector near the fuel tank

checks: Measure the vent valve resistance
Inspect the wiring under the vehicle near the tank
fix: Usually a new vent valve or a wiring repair.

title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
plain: The circuit for the EVAP vent valve is reading higher voltage than it should, often from an open wire or failed valve.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
checks: Measure the vent valve resistance
Check the connector near the tank for corrosion
fix: Usually a new vent valve or a wiring repair.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Flow
plain: On engines with a second EGR valve or path, the computer sees too much or too little exhaust flow through it.
symptoms: Possible rough running or reduced power

causes.name: Carbon or soot clogging the EGR "B" path

checks: Command EGR valve "B" with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve and passages for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B" and its passages.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Flow Insufficient Detected
plain: Too little exhaust is flowing through the second EGR valve or path.
checks: Command EGR valve "B" with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve and passages for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning passages or replacing EGR valve "B".

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Flow Excessive Detected
plain: Too much exhaust is flowing through the second EGR valve or path, often because the valve is stuck open.
checks: Command EGR valve "B" with a scan tool and compare actual position
Inspect the valve and passages for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B".

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "A" Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
plain: The computer learns where the EGR valve closed position is. That learned position has drifted outside the allowed range, usually from carbon buildup or a worn valve.

causes.name: Carbon or soot buildup on the EGR valve seat
Faulty position sensor in the valve

checks: Remove and inspect the EGR valve for buildup
Run the EGR relearn with a scan tool after cleaning or replacing
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR valve, then running a relearn.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "B" Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
plain: The learned closed position of the second EGR valve has drifted outside the allowed range, usually from carbon buildup or wear.

causes.name: Carbon or soot buildup on the valve seat
Faulty position sensor in the valve

checks: Remove and inspect the valve for buildup
Run the EGR relearn with a scan tool after the repair
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing EGR valve "B", then running a relearn.

title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve "B"
plain: On engines with a second exhaust pressure control valve, the computer sees a problem with that valve or its circuit.
symptoms: Possible loss of power on diesels

causes.name: Valve seized by soot or rust

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch it move
Inspect the wiring and connector
fix: Usually a new valve or actuator, or a wiring repair.
